entries.mechanism: Whole-dollar rounding-chain divergence between axiom's 7 CFR 273.10(e)(1)(ii)/(e)(2)(ii)(A) rounding elections and PolicyEngine's cents-precision convention, compounding across three stages for this one-person all-earned-income unit (gross 774.427979, standard deduction 209, shelter costs 594 = the CO heating/cooling SUA, maximum allotment 298; both engines agree on all four). (1) Earned income deduction: both start from 20% x 774.427979 = 154.885596; axiom drops cents to 154 (rulespec-us us/regulations/7-cfr/273/10.yaml snap_earned_income_deduction_for_net_income = floor(earned x rate), matching the FNS QC FSERNDED construction), while PE's snap_earned_income_deduction keeps 154.885596. (2) Excess shelter deduction: axiom rounds 594 - 0.5 x (774.427979 - 209 - 154) = 388.286011 to the nearest dollar, 388 (snap_excess_shelter_cost = floor(x + 0.5), the 273.10(e)(1)(ii)(A) election); PE keeps 594 - 0.5 x (774.427979 - 209 - 154.885596) = 388.728821 in cents (snap_excess_shelter_expense_deduction, no rounding). Both engines' evidence net incomes reproduce exactly: axiom 774.427979 - 209 - 154 - 388 = 23.427979, PE 774.427979 - 209 - 154.885596 - 388.728821 = 21.813538. (3) Allotment: axiom applies Colorado's round-the-allotment-down election (rulespec-us-co regulations/10-ccr-2506-1/4.207.2.yaml sets state_agency_rounds_thirty_percent_net_income_up = false, so snap_calculated_monthly_allotment_before_minimums = floor(298 - 0.3 x 23.427979) = floor(290.971606) = 290); PE instead floors net income to whole dollars and keeps the 30% product in cents (snap_expected_contribution = np.floor(snap_net_income) x 0.3 at policyengine-us 1.705.1, snap_normal_allotment subtracts it unrounded): 298 - 0.3 x floor(21.813538) = 298 - 6.3 = 291.70, printed 291.700012 in float32. Both are readings of 7 CFR 273.10(e); axiom's whole-dollar elections match what a state agency issues, PE's is a documented cents-precision modeling convention (291.70 is not an issuable whole-dollar allotment). The residual is exactly 290 - 291.700012 = -1.700012. The suite tolerance of 1.5 absorbs single-stage rounding differences; this case exceeds it only because the three stages compound in the same direction.
